look_here_first: Start with the tiny linear leaves. Narrowleaf elbowbush is densely twiggy with stiff 90-degree branching and very narrow leathery, often slightly rolled leaves. That skeletal, almost olive-like foliage separates it quickly from the broader-leaved F. pubescens.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Travis — City of Austin environmental assessment in Travis County explicitly lists F. angustifolia; Uvalde — Harris Ranch vegetation study records the species; Bexar — archaeological/environmental vegetation documentation lists elbow bush F. angustifolia.

best_field_traits: evergreen to semi-evergreen shrub, drought-deciduous in severe dryness
dense intricate branching with stiff near-right-angle branchlets
leaf margins entire and often revolute
young twigs dark; older bark smooth gray
inconspicuous green-yellow apetalous flowers before new leaves
morphology_keys.comparison_training: F. pubescens has much broader elliptic/ovate leaves with more visible pubescence and a winter-deciduous habit; F. angustifolia is the narrow, skeletal-leaved shrub.

comparisons.key_distinctions: F. pubescens has much broader elliptic/ovate leaves with more visible pubescence and a winter-deciduous habit; F. angustifolia is the narrow, skeletal-leaved shrub.
